name: Column
description: A titled column of cards, as on the Ringmaster board's desktop: a rounded surface a step off the page, a 32 px header (optional glyph, an h2 title, a CountBadge count, optional marks, an action pushed right) and the cards 24 px apart. `scroll` makes the body scroll inside a height you give, under a header that stays put.
usage: Several side by side in a grid on desktop (the board's: grid items-start gap-sm, 1fr 1fr 1.2fr); one per page inside a ColumnStrip on a phone
A number `count` renders a plain CountBadge; pass a CountBadge element for another look (tone="caution", a label)
`icon` is decorative: the title says it. Give the glyph aria-hidden
Drag and drop is yours: put a SortableList (inside your SortableGroup) in the children
`scroll`: give the column a bounded height (a fixed height, or a flex/grid parent with one); it fills it with h-full and its body scrolls. Without `scroll` the column is as tall as its cards
examples: } action={}>{cards} …
design: Dark: --color-surface-section. Light: --color-border-subtle, a step below the page, as the board does: every levain light surface is lighter than the page and there is no sunken surface token yet (GAPS)
Corners: --radius-lg + 4 px, the cards' radius plus a step
Header 32 px, 14 px medium, items 8 px apart, inset 36 px so the title lines up with the cards' text; the body 12 px in from the column's edge, 8 px under the header
accessibility: A section named by `title` (a region), with the title as its h2
The count is read as its number unless you pass a CountBadge with a `label`

props.name: title
props.description: The h2, and the region's accessible name

props.name: count
props.description: A number becomes a plain CountBadge; an element is rendered as given; 0 shows

props.name: marks
props.description: After the count: small marks or tags

props.name: action
props.description: A control at the header's right end

props.name: scroll
props.description: The body scrolls inside the height you give; the header stays put
